message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  

**What you can do instead:**

| Source | How to use it | Typical data shown |
|--------|---------------|--------------------|
| **AirNow (U.S. EPA)** | Go to https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), forecast for the next 24 h. |
| **EPA Air Quality Index app** | Download the free app on iOS/Android. | Real‑time AQI, health recommendations, alerts. |
| **Local news websites** | Check the weather/air‑quality section. | Often include a quick AQI snapshot and any health advisories. |
| **Weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather)** | Look for the “Air Quality” tab. | Current AQI, pollutant levels, forecast. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check one of those sources right before you head out. If you need help interpreting the AQI numbers or want to know what the different pollutant levels mean for health, just let me know!
